method: Static analysis only: original-byte PyInstaller/CAB extraction, xdis Python 3.7 disassembly, LSB/AES recovery, Donut instance Chaskey-CTR decryption, aPLib decompression, native export/xref/control-flow analysis, UTF16 Base64 PowerShell recovery. No specimen code executed.

verdicts.marker_line: PyInstaller loader: LSB/AES shellcode execution; add linked traits
AutoHotkey CAB: downloads and injects APC payloads; add detection
zlibxjson 8.2 wheel: confirmed malware; hidden EXE launcher
zlibxjson main: downloads Discord EXE to APPDATA and hides launch

archive_policy: Retain the user-confirmed malicious archive verdicts; examine component code individually. main.py is malicious independently of the wheel label. Bundled library/interpreter capabilities are not attributed to first-party code.

pyinstaller: The actual script entry is loader (Python 3.7 marshaled bytecode). Its __main__ block first copies xunlei.exe, ahk.exe, b64 and bd to Public Downloads. Missing-copy exceptions are caught, so the absent bd does not block main.

main reads the resource selected by --file (default: an MP3-named blob). Indexed one-bit extraction reconstructs a big-endian length, then 397024 bytes. It splits these into a 16-byte IV, 16-byte AES key and CBC ciphertext, decrypts and unpads.

The 396984-byte result is passed to len, VirtualAlloc with MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE and PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, then memmove. CFUNCTYPE(None) wraps that very pointer, the resulting local is immediately called. The new bytecode rules verify the copied pointer, wrapper local, and decrypt-result/copy-source operands, rather than relying on function names.

The native shellcode starts with a relative call around an encrypted Donut instance. Chaskey-CTR decryption from instance offset 572 yields an embedded native DLL module, aPLib compressed. Decompression produces 763392 bytes, SHA256 09f45f76eb7de08d71d26b79c32aa392b604ddab3580cc9fa5e7176a9d205eac. Method configuration selects export KKHS; bypass is 1, so standard Donut AMSI/ETW bypass support is not claimed as enabled.

KKHS enumerates processes for 360Tray.exe and checks HipsTray.exe. Native paths reference the staged b64 file, construct a minimized PowerShell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass command that decodes the file as UTF16 Base64 and invokes it, launch/drop AutoHotkey automation, and terminate client.exe. These observations come from resolved xrefs and execution paths, not just strings.

The b64 member decodes to PowerShell containing an embedded native stage, VirtualAlloc RWX, Marshal.Copy to its allocated pointer, CreateThread using that pointer, and WaitForSingleObject. Its beginning is corrupted; later source is recoverable. The new encoded API profile deliberately asserts references only, not successful script execution.
cab: temp.ahk is executable AHK v2 source despite being analyzed as text. It hides its tray, prioritizes execution, and discovers Telegram through a WMI process query before invoking a language-change URL.

Three jobs target rundll32.exe or WmiPrvSE.exe. Two actual URLs are Base64 decoded via CryptStringToBinary; one hides a different endpoint than the display URL. The script constructs WinHttpRequest, GETs each URL, accesses ResponseBody and copies its bytes to a buffer.

InjectShellcode creates the target suspended (flag 4), allocates remote RWX memory, writes the response bytes, queues that address with QueueUserAPC on the new primary thread and resumes it. Timers retry each unfinished job every second. On failure it closes handles and may terminate the newly created process; successful completion exits the script.
The actual remote-write/APC/resume relationship establishes injection; the bundled AutoHotkey interpreter is separate. No persistence, exfiltration or later payload effect is inferred.
zlibxjson: __init__.py only exports init. Installation or ordinary import does not invoke the downloader; console entry zlibxjson_command maps to main:init.

init reads APPDATA and passes it with a fixed Discord attachment EXE URL to download_file. The helper creates the destination if needed, strips the URL query for the filename, streams requests.get chunks to that same binary file, and returns the path.

init passes the returned path to run_silently. subprocess.Popen launches it with shell=True and CREATE_NO_WINDOW; exceptions print a diagnostic. No signature/hash validation or JSON/compression implementation is present.

The sole hidden executable-launch purpose and placeholder package provenance tip the individual malicious judgment. Original deployment authorization, runtime success and downstream EXE behavior are unknown. No obfuscation, persistence, theft, escalation or cleanup exists in this member.

recovery_limits.all_wheels: forager fetch --all-wheels pkg:pypi/zlibxjson@8.2: PyPI metadata 404; browser fallback cannot start because ICU data is unavailable. Original supplied wheel and exact member bytes remain available.
recovery_limits.discord_payload: Exact signed URL attempted with forager: HTTP 404.
recovery_limits.automatic_analysis: The original scanner does not automatically reconstruct the LSB/AES/Chaskey/aPLib stages. Large standalone Base64 blobs also exceed its decoded-string path; direct Base64-of-UTF16 YARA API patterns now cover the sidecar without claiming its invocation succeeds.

rule_changes: Add neutral AHK HTTP construction, text-to-binary decoding, remote executable allocation, remote write, APC scheduling and thread-resume observations; generalize the existing typed suspended-creation argument to support AHK and AutoIt.
Add an APC injection objective requiring suspended creation, remote RWX allocation/write, APC queueing and thread resume within 2300 bytes.

Add native-pointer invocation and nested-result/copy operand relationships, CBC decrypt member and VirtualAlloc references, and one-bit extraction/shift-packing wordcode observations. Add distinct hostile native-payload activation and low-bit-concealment composites.
Add a suspicious Base64-of-UTF16 allocation/copy/thread API profile for the sidecar. This is a reference profile, not an execution or transport claim.

Relocate vba-wmi-win32-process-binding to micro-behaviors/os/wmi/query::win32-process-class-fragment. Preserve matcher, scope, confidence and notable severity; update its exact consumer. The old name claimed VBA and its dropper placement implied intent unsupported by a generic WMI class substring. Remove the inherited execution/download ATT&CK/MBC mappings: the class-name substring establishes none of those actions.

shared_rule_audit.wmi: Exact consumer and ancestor-selector search performed. Same substring, scope and confidence retained; the Office macro objective references the new neutral ID. External WSH/HTA attack fixtures and benign process-event/startup controls preserve all findings after migration mapping.
shared_rule_audit.ffi: No exact consumers of the old AutoIt ID existed. The typed argument matcher is widened, with original dword/decimal4 syntax retained and UInt/0x4/multiline variants accepted. Numeric40 is a near miss. Criticality remains notable. No old attack coverage is erased to meet a directory budget.

checks.result: All passed; no mapped finding loss on consumer fixtures. Full original/member deltas are in comparison.json.
checks.final_validation_command: make validate (run after all markers and review artifacts)

hostile_coverage_limits.exe: Two distinct hostile rules, not three. Payload activation and low-bit concealment are covered. Hidden native-stage process gating, staged interpreter launches and process termination are documented but not automatically exposed as decoded files by the scanner; original-layer rules cannot honestly assert those deeper operations without reconstruction. The encoded sidecar is covered at suspicious API-profile severity.
hostile_coverage_limits.cab: One hostile rule covers the one supported APC injection mechanism. Decoding, network retrieval, allocation/write and thread resume are also detected at notable severity. No separate persistence/theft/destruction objective exists; three near-identical injection composites would duplicate the same behavior. Unknown fetched payload bytes prevent downstream objective coverage.
hostile_coverage_limits.main: Zero hostile and two suspicious, intentionally retained. The linked download-and-hidden-launch mechanics overlap legitimate updaters; placeholder package context supports the human verdict but cannot justify three hostile primitives or a filename-based conviction. The downstream EXE is unavailable.

classifier_disagreement: The PE strengthens from FP level1 to0; CAB stays level0. main.py and the wheel remain weakly alerted only at level5000/confidence54, despite the malicious human judgment. The older v18 feature specification does not contain all v21 engine features. No inaccurate or duplicate hostile traits were added to raise these scores.
baseline_control: Final comparisons use a git-HEAD rules snapshot with slow/local/no-update/--follow=none on identical input bytes. Initial exploratory --follow none was parsed as a bare --follow plus a nonexistent path none; its URL-follow recomputation added derived notable observations to standalone main.py. That run is retained in scratch but excluded from controlled deltas.
